observations: Oak6 is a slender branching sapling; oak30 develops a broad irregular crown with a dense twig-heavy interior.
Oak18 has an irregular spreading crown with attached terminal leaf clusters; multiple viewing angles retain the branch silhouette.
Ash18 has more upward branching and compound foliage, while birch18 is sparser with downward laterals.
Spruce18 retains a leader and repeated lateral branches. Full-tree needle coverage is sparse; a 0.4m close-up confirms rendered three-dimensional needles on shoots.
All species still show long straight internodes and angular changes. Species profiles require further visual calibration; no botanical-fidelity or superiority acceptance is claimed.
